glossary.hospital admission: Being taken in to hospital as an inpatient; the clock for hospital-acquired infection starts here.
glossary.community source: An infection picked up outside hospital before admission.
glossary.hospitalisation: Being in hospital, which itself exposes patients to resistant organisms.
glossary.indwelling devices: Equipment left inside the body, such as urinary catheters and central lines.
glossary.catheter: A tube placed into the body, often into the bladder to drain urine.
glossary.central lines: Catheters placed in a large central vein for drugs, fluids or monitoring.
glossary.immunosuppression: A weakened immune system, from disease or drugs such as steroids or chemotherapy.
glossary.dysuria: Pain or burning when passing urine.
glossary.wound discharge: Fluid or pus leaking from a surgical or other wound.
glossary.positive culture: Growth of an organism from a sample such as blood, urine or sputum.
glossary.resistant: Not killed by antibiotics that would normally work.
glossary.RR: Respiratory rate: breaths per minute; normal adult is about 12 to 20.
glossary.hypoxia: Low oxygen levels in the blood or tissues.
glossary.SpO2: Oxygen saturation measured by a pulse oximeter on the finger.
glossary.saturations: Percentage of haemoglobin carrying oxygen, measured by pulse oximetry.
glossary.bloodstream infection: Bacteria growing in the blood (bacteraemia), often from a line.
glossary.blood cultures: Bottles of blood incubated to grow and identify bacteria causing sepsis.
glossary.urine culture: Growing bacteria from a urine sample to identify a UTI and its sensitivities.
glossary.sputum culture: Growing organisms from coughed-up phlegm to identify a chest infection.
glossary.CT: Computed tomography: a cross-sectional X-ray scan.
glossary.FBC: Full blood count, including white cell count.
glossary.broad-spectrum: Active against a wide range of bacteria.
glossary.lower respiratory tract samples: Sputum or bronchial washings from the airways below the larynx.
glossary.peripheral blood cultures: Blood cultures taken from a vein by fresh needle, not through an existing line.
glossary.recurrence: The infection coming back after treatment.
glossary.hand hygiene: Washing or gelling hands before and after patient contact to stop spread of bacteria.
glossary.medical emergency: A condition needing immediate treatment to prevent death or serious harm.
glossary.host: The patient whose body the organism infects.
glossary.microbial flora: The community of bacteria and other microbes living in a place or body site.
glossary.anatomical barriers: Skin and mucous membranes that normally keep bacteria out.
glossary.host immunity: The patient's own immune defences against infection.
glossary.gut flora: The normal bacteria living in the bowel that keep C. difficile in check.
glossary.spores: Tough dormant forms of bacteria that survive alcohol gel and spread on wards.
glossary.germinate: For a spore, to wake up and become an active, multiplying bacterium.
glossary.oropharyngeal secretions: Saliva and mucus from the mouth and throat.
glossary.cuff: The inflatable balloon near the tip of an endotracheal tube that seals the airway.
glossary.ventilator: A machine that breathes for a patient through a tube in the airway.
glossary.affinity: How tightly a drug binds its target.
